newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bourse slips, focus on Woodchester.
newsitem.headline: Irish bourse slips, focus on Woodchester.

text.p: The Irish bourse ended marginally down on Wednesday, despite good interest in financial stocks, particularly Woodchester which is expected to reveal more than its results, due on Thursday, dealers said.

There is mounting speculation that Woodchester will use the announcement of its 1996 results as an opportunity to clarify what will happen to its 54 percent shareholding held by troubled french banking group Crdit Lyonnais.
"Woodchester is in very good demand ahead of the presentation of results tonight and tomorrow morning" one dealer said.

Financial services group Woodchester, which will meet with fund managers at 2000 GMT on Wednesday, is expected to tell shareholders that advisers have been appointed to find a buyer for the company who will invite offers from suitable purchasers.
Elsewhere in the market dealers said leading financial stocks were generally strong with AIB and Bank of Ireland both up on the day.

"The story is one of very strong financials and nothing happening at all in the industrial stocks," the dealer said. "Good demand for both AIB and Bank of Ireland drove both those share prices higher."
AIB gained three pence to 453 and Bank of Ireland rose
4.5 pence to 652. Irish Life was unchanged at 331, while Irish Permanent was up five pence at 625.
Among leading industrials, food stock Avonmore remained unchanged at 235 while CRH gained one pence to 652. Kerry Group was flat at 655.
Trading on the Irish bourse on Wednesday was around the levels of Tuesday's session, up on Monday, at around 35-40 million Irish pounds, dealers said.
By 1759 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was down 4.12 points or 0.13 percent at 3,055.51.
